evidence: tests/sentry/api/endpoints/test_organization_auditlogs.py has no reference to optimized_pagination/OptimizedCursorPaginator, and tests/sentry/api/test_paginator.py only has test_negative_offset for OffsetPaginator (line 143). Tests are needed here: the new path crashes on any non-empty page (see id 7), negative offsets raise (ids 6/8), and member=None crashes (id 5). A basic endpoint test would have caught all of these.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 reads request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true" directly, while event/actor go through AuditLogQueryParamSerializer (lines 22-31, 52-57). Putting a BooleanField on the serializer would be more consistent and would also accept 1/True. But the raw string check is not a correctness or security problem: a value that doesn't match just falls back to DateTimePaginator.

src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-28: the PR only adds a comment above the existing self.offset = int(offset). Cursor.__init__ never validated the sign, so the comment ('Allow negative offsets...') describes no behavior change and suggests a feature that downstream querysets don't support (Django rejects negative slices). The comment is misleading and should be removed.

The concern about this code is justified: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877-882 (OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result) passes cursor.offset < 0 straight to queryset[start_offset:stop], with comments saying it 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds'. The claimed effect is wrong, though. Django 5.2.1 (requirements-frozen.txt:36) QuerySet.__getitem__ raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.') before any SQL runs. The queryset is also scoped to organization_id (organization_auditlogs.py:48). So the result is a 500 error, not access to other data. The negative-offset branch should still be removed.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:834-836: __init__(..., enable_advanced_features=False) followed by self.enable_advanced_features = enable_advanced_features is the standard Python idiom for storing a constructor argument on the instance. There is no shadowing bug and no ambiguity. The same pattern is used throughout BasePaginator.__init__ (lines 59-74: queryset, max_limit, on_results, post_query_filter).

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 evaluates organization_context.member.has_global_access, but RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is typed RpcOrganizationMember | None and the model says 'member can be None when the given user_id does not have membership' (src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/model.py:344-346). The reviewer's superuser example is wrong: `request.user.is_superuser or ...` short-circuits for superusers. A caller that passes OrganizationAuditPermission without membership and is not a superuser, such as a token-authenticated integration or proxy user, gets an AttributeError. This line runs on every request, even without optimized_pagination=true, so the default path can crash too. Fix: guard with `organization_context.member is not None` and compute it only when use_optimized is set.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182-184: start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset, then queryset[start_offset:stop]. Negative slicing is indeed unsupported, but Django 5.2.1 (requirements-frozen.txt:36) raises ValueError, not AssertionError. In BasePaginator the change clamps the non-prev path to 0, which makes it safer. The is_prev path still slices with the raw offset as before, so a crafted cursor such as '1:-5:1' (Cursor.from_string, cursors.py:53-61) still causes a 500. That is mostly pre-existing behavior. The added comment ('This is safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions') is factually wrong and should be corrected.

organization_auditlogs.py:76-83 uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime'. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key (paginator.py:838-840) calls math.floor/ceil on getattr(item, 'datetime'), which raises TypeError for a datetime. build_cursor always calls key() on results (cursors.py:122,137,197), so every non-empty first page fails. value_from_cursor (paginator.py:842-843) returns a raw int, which build_queryset (lines 112-126) then compares against the datetime column. Compare DateTimePaginator (lines 230-241), which converts both ways. As written, the optimized path cannot work for this endpoint.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:874-882: the comment 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false. Django 5.2.1 QuerySet.__getitem__ raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.') for a negative slice start. With enable_advanced_features=True, which the endpoint always passes at organization_auditlogs.py:82, any cursor with a negative offset returns a 500. The branch is broken and should be removed.

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:845-911) is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result (lines 136-215). The only difference is the negative-offset branch at 877-882, which is itself broken (ids 3/8). Its get_item_key and value_from_cursor (838-843) duplicate Paginator (lines 221-227). Once the negative-offset branch is removed, the class adds nothing over Paginator/DateTimePaginator, so the duplication should go away. Severity is lower than the correctness bugs.
